title: NAME OF THE SHEET
sub: The six, in one line: what to lead and the sets to train.
leads_intro: Pick the lead at team preview, then the turn-one line for what they send out. Percentages are how often to click each line; use any randomizer. The two numbers are your win chance after turn one against how the Showdown ladder clicks, then against a player who reads your mix; red means the lead loses turn one.

Each tab shows the four to bring: the lead and back row that won the most whole-game sims against that archetype (both sides switching, every turn played out, endgames included). Its lines are the turn-one plan for that lead.
leads_method: The lead and back row shown won the most whole-game sims: full 4v4 battles in a native port of Showdown’s engine, both sides playing each turn’s best mix (switches included) to the end, against the archetype’s six most common leads with the back rows they bring in 5,000 Showdown M-C Bo3 replays. Every four of the six was tried, and the leaders were replayed head to head on fresh games. The turn-one lines were run with 12 RNG samples per cell in Showdown’s engine with Champions mechanics and scored with a win model fit on 7,781 games. Their Indeedee F’s item is mixed at replay rates: Rocky Helmet 48%, Colbur Berry 32%, Psychic Seed 20%. Their other leads are not simulated.
team_intro: Stat points (SP) are what you assign in the game; the stat row is the result at level 50, after Mega Evolution for the Mega.
cov_intro: Your hardest hit on each threat, worst gaps first. Pessimistic throughout: each threat is at the bulkiest of its most common spreads for the side you hit, with the items that stop a knockout: Focus Sash (Arcanine-H, Pelipper, Whimsicott), Chople on Kingambit, Colbur on Indeedee F. Sitrus is never counted as extra HP, and Sneasler has already used its Grassy Seed (+1 Defense). The threat’s own weather and terrain are up, and yours where one of your Pokémon sets it by ability. Spread moves take their 25% cut, and Fake Out is left out. Tap a row for every attacker.
One-hit KOs only, so “none” can still be a clean two-hit win; the Matchups grid counts those.
mx_intro: Who wins the one-on-one with both sides picking their best move each turn: your minimum rolls against their maximum, across their most-used spreads, up to three. Switch between no Trick Room and Trick Room up for the whole fight. Tap a row for the numbers. Under each name: its op.gg doubles usage or ladder rank.
mx_foot: One-on-one only, Protect left out. Fake Out is in, on each side’s first turn out; it can’t touch Ghost types, and Psychic Terrain blocks it and every other priority move. “Trick Room up” keeps it up for the whole fight. Spread damage is in, partner chip is not; in doubles, chip is what breaks the * wins. Rolls count accuracy as 100%. Their Pelipper, Charizard Y, Torkoal and Tyranitar bring their weather; Grassy Terrain is up against Rillaboom and a seeded Sneasler, and their Psychic Terrain against Indeedee. A partner’s weather or terrain is never assumed on your side. Mega Raichu Y’s Zap Cannon always paralyses: your worst luck counts every turn as fully paralysed, and real rolls use Champions’ 1-in-8 chance. A Mega takes its switch-in hit before it Mega Evolves.
speed_intro: Fastest first. Your six are shaded; the others are the most common opposing spreads on the Showdown ladder (Smogon’s September 2026 Reg M-C stats), named by nature and the Speed points the spread uses. Equal numbers are a coin flip.
footer: Damage. Coverage and Matchups use an exact damage calculator that follows Showdown’s formula, checked against the Smogon calculator, without crits. The leads were simulated in Showdown’s own engine with Champions mechanics.
